BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.claim: The deniers, especially Meccan unbelievers, will think at the Hour that they had stayed only a single evening or morning after being warned.
BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.anchor: أي المنكرين وبالفارسية كوييا كفار مكة

BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.claim: Duha is the period from sunrise until noon; the short span refers to part of one day, with evening and morning linked by their belonging to the same day.
BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.anchor: الضحى اسم لما بين إشراق الشمس إلى استواء النهار ثم هي عشى إلى الغداة

QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.claim: The evening or morning may mean the setting of truth’s light in bodies or its rising from the west; witnessing resurrection through unity makes worldly existence seem only imagined.
QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.anchor: وقت غروب نور الحق في الأجساد أو وقت طلوعه من مغربه

QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.claim: Alternatively, the two brief spans are bodily and spiritual worlds, concealed by sensation and intellect; passing both is described as two steps before arrival.
QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.anchor: في عالم الأجسام والاحتجاب بالحس أو في عالم الأرواح والاحتجاب بالعقل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.claim: The Prophet should not be troubled by demands for the Hour’s timing: only God knows it, the Prophet’s duty is warning, and at its sight people will feel they stayed only a short while.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.anchor: The time of arrival of the Day of Judgement is something which only the Almighty knows

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.claim: At Judgment, people will see that their worldly stay seemed no longer than an evening or morning, so its arrival should not be dismissed as distant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.anchor: more than the first or last part of a day

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.claim: Qatada says people regard their worldly stay as short once they witness the afterlife.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها ﴾ قال استقلوا لما عاينوا الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.claim: The brief-life comparison brings the Hour close: they will think they lived only an afternoon or its morning, with day-end terms joined by expansive إضافة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.anchor: كأنهم يوم يرونها: تقريب وتقرير لقصر مقامهم في الدنيا.

FARRA:v3p234/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p234/r4.claim: Evening can mean the end and morning the beginning, so Arabic can pair evening with its next morning or morning with its preceding evening.
FARRA:v3p234/r4.anchor: فهذا بين ظاهر من كلام العرب أن يقولوا: آتيك العشية أو غداتها،

FARRA:v3p234/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r5.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
FARRA:v3p234/r5.claim: A poet of Banū ʿUqayl uses ʿashiyyat al-hilāl for the evening of the crescent's setting, supporting the time-pairing idiom.
FARRA:v3p234/r5.anchor: أنشدني بعض بني عقيل: نحن صبحنا عامرا في دارها ... عشية الهلال أو سرارها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.claim: The likeness either confirms the warning that the Hour will arrive swiftly, or answers mockers who impatiently ask when it will come: after the warning they will have waited only briefly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.anchor: إما تقرير وتأكيد لما ينبيء عنه الإنذار من سرعة مجيء المنذر به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.claim: The compact wording replaces “only an hour of the day, its evening or forenoon”; possessive suffixes rule out imagining an interval from one day's evening until another day's forenoon.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.anchor: على ما نقل عن الزمخشري له أصل وهو لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار عشيته أو ضحاه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.claim: Al-Tibi allows evening or forenoon to stand metaphorically for the whole day; adding the pronoun reinforces this and excludes the broader possibility, like saying one saw something with one's own eyes.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.anchor: وقال الطيبي إنه من المحتمل أن يراد بالعشية أو الضحى كل اليوم مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.claim: Alusi prefers the less forced explanation of the added pronoun, while allowing it to reinforce the whole-day interpretation too; he takes the interval as worldly life for some and the grave for others.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.anchor: ولكن السابق أبعد من التكلف ولا منع من الجمع وزاد الإضافة حسنا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.claim: The context calls for a short stay after the warning or threat, which both makes the warning real and rebuts their impatient challenge; the sentence is circumstantial on one reading and independent on the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.anchor: اعتبار كونه بعد الإنذار أو بعد الوعيد تحقيقا للإنذار وردا لاستبطائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.claim: Connecting “what place are you in regarding its reminder?” as a substitute for their question, or as their quoted words, is weak; the direct answer is that the Hour's endpoint belongs to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى ضعف ذلك وأخراج البزار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet was repeatedly asked about the Hour until 79:43–44 was revealed, after which he stopped asking about it; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.anchor: وصححه عن عائشة قالت ما زال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يسأل عن الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.speaker: طارق بن شهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.claim: Tariq ibn Shihab reports that the Prophet often mentioned the Hour until 79:43–44 was revealed and then refrained from mentioning it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.anchor: عن طارق بن شهاب قال كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يكثر ذكر الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة وخالد الحذاء وابن هرمز وعيسى وطلحة وابن محيصن وابن مقسم وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.claim: These readers, in a report from al-Mundhir, read mundhir with tanwīn and make it govern its object; the construction is original, while genitive attachment can also serve lightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة وخالد الحذاء وابن هرمز وعيسى وطلحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.claim: The ‘they’ are Quraysh unbelievers, who will see Resurrection and feel they spent only an evening or its dawn on earth; another view places the short stay in their graves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.anchor: {كأنهم} يعني كفار قريش {يوم يرونها} يعاينون يوم القيامة {لم يلبثوا} في الدنيا، وقيل: في قبورهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.claim: Al-Farra notes evening has no literal dawn; this is an Arabic expression for the last or first part of a day, as in the comparison to an hour of a day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: (2) ليس للعشية ضحى، إنما الضحى لصدر النهار، ولكن هذا ظاهر من كلام العرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.claim: When they see it, worldly life or their grave-stay seems no longer than an evening or its morning, as in 46:35; evening and morning belong to one day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.anchor: { كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا } في الدنيا أو في القبور. { إلا عشية أو ضحها }

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.claim: A report promises that a reciter of Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt will be held at resurrection only as long as an obligatory prayer before entering Paradise; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.anchor: من قرأ سورة النازعات كان ممن حبسه الله في القيامة حتى يدخل الجنة قدر صلاة المكتوبة

BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.claim: Qur'anic uses include duha opposite evening, the sun's light brought forth, and a specific time appointed for events; these usages weigh against interpreting it as the whole day.
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.anchor: وفي الاستعمال القرآني، نرى القرآن الكريم استعمل الضحى مقابلاً للعشية

NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.claim: People will feel they scarcely remained; this warns worldly people that they soon leave their pleasures as if they stayed only an evening or morning.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.anchor: وكان في هذا معنى التنبيه لمن اغتر بالدنيا وسلامته فيها في أنه سيتركها عن قليل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.claim: The name al-Nāziʿāt points to angels extracting souls and then the account of Pharaoh and Moses; al-Sāhirah and al-Ṭāmmah also fit the oath and the surah’s flow.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.anchor: وصور ذلك بنزع الأرواح بأيدي الملائكة الكرام ، ثم أمر فرعون اللعين وموسى عليه السلام ، واسمها النازعات واضح في ذلك المرام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r6.claim: At the Hour, people will think their stay in the world and graves lasted only part of a day: from noon to sunset, or from morning until noon.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.claim: The comparison belittles worldly time against the limitless afterlife; the Prophet likens this world’s share to a finger dipped in the sea and withdrawn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.anchor: وهذا تعبير لنا بما نحسه تقريبا لعقولنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.claim: Disbelievers give differing estimates of their stay, but the truth is that their past seems like a brief hour beside the endless future they face.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.anchor: على أن الكفار أيضا يستقصرون مدة لبثهم , فكأنهم أصناف : بعضهم يقول : إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.claim: The comparison recalls the judgment scene where people say they stayed only an hour, or answer that they remained a day or part of one and defer to the counters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.anchor: كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.claim: The surah closes by returning from resurrection to its opening, then connects to the next surah through fear and remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.anchor: فقد رجع آخرها بالقيامة على أولها , والتف مفصلها بنزع الأنفس اللوامة على موصلها , واتصلت بأول ما بعدها من جهة الخشية والتذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.claim: The report that some answer “a day or part of a day” is linked to the question about years in al-Muʾminūn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.anchor: كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم اسأل العادين

DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.claim: Anas transmits a prayer for success that invokes God's mercy, forgiveness, safety, good deeds, Paradise, and deliverance from Hell, and includes the two verses about the briefness of worldly time.

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r4.claim: Aisha reports that when visiting Bedouins asked about the Hour, the Prophet pointed to the youngest person and said that if he lived a century, their own Hour would have come.

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the Hour's endpoint as God's knowledge and interprets the brief evening and morning as worldly time.
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.anchor: ابن المنذر عن ابن جرير في قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.claim: Qatada says worldly life will seem slight to people when they see the affair of the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {كأنهم يوم يرونها}

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.claim: At the Hour's sight, a person will feel that no more than an evening or its morning had passed; الضحى is attached to العشية for brevity as the day's two ends.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.anchor: ثم قرب تعالى أمر الساعة بإخباره أن الإنسان عند رؤيته إياها لم يلبث إلا عشية يوم أو بكرته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.claim: Quraysh's unbelievers will feel, on seeing the Resurrection, as if they had remained in worldly life or their graves for only an evening or its first part.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.anchor: يعني كفار قريش يوم يرونها أي يعاينون القيامه لم يلبثوا في الدنيا وقيل في قبورهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.claim: The pronouns in ḍuḥāhā refer to al-ʿashiyya, so the phrase means the evening's own early part.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.anchor: والهاء والألف في ضحاها عائدان إلى العشية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.claim: The phrase means the evening's ḍuḥā; Arabic can pair evening with its morning-side or morning with its evening-side to refer to the respective ends of a period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.anchor: إلا عشية أو ضحى العشية قال الفراء فإن قيل للعشية ضحى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.claim: A cited poem says they attacked ʿĀmir at evening, at the new moon's setting or its hidden phase, illustrating the idiom's evening expression.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.anchor: نحن صبحنا عامرا في دارها عشية الهلال أو سرارها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.claim: When raised from their graves, people will consider worldly life so brief it seemed like part of one afternoon or morning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.anchor: إذا قاموا من قبورهم إلى المحشر يستقصرون مدة الحياة الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas defines evening as noon to sunset and morning as sunrise to noon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.anchor: قال جويبر، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: {كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها} أما عشية: فما بين الظهر إلى غروب الشمس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.claim: Qatada says the whole duration of worldly life will seem brief when people behold the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: وقت الدنيا في أعين القوم حين عاينوا الآخرة.

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.claim: These verses also demonstrate the Resurrection's tremendous condition and many terrors.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.anchor: وتدل على عظيم حال القيامة، وكثرة أهوالها

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.claim: People will regard worldly life as brief when they witness the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.anchor: ومنها: أنهم يستقلون الدنيا عند معاينته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.claim: People seem to have lived in the world—or in the graves—only an evening or its morning; adding the morning to evening marks less than a full day, just an hour of it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.anchor: كأنهم لم يلبثوا في الدنيا ، وقيل : في القبور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.claim: A report promises that whoever recites Surat al-Nazi'at will be held in the grave and at the Resurrection only as long as an obligatory prayer, then enter Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة والنازعات كان ممن حبسه الله في القبر والقيامة حتى يدخل الجنة قدر صلاة المكتوبة

SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.claim: ‘Aw duha-ha’ means the bright part of its evening; it figuratively attaches one time expression to another, naming the two ends of the day, and the cadence favors the construction.
SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.anchor: أي: ضحى العشية، أضاف الظرف إلى ضمير الظرف الآخر تجوزا واتساعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.claim: They are disbelievers seeing the afterlife; they feel they stayed in the world only an afternoon or its morning, since worldly life shrinks in retrospect, as in Quran 10:45.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.anchor: في الدنيا . { إلا عشية } وهي ما بعد الزوال

MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.claim: When people see the Hour, they will think they stayed amid worldly life and pleasure for only an evening from afternoon to sunset or a morning until the sun rises higher.
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.anchor: إلا عشية } وهي مابين صلاة العصر وإلى أن تغيب الشمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.claim: At the Hour, people will think they stayed in this world only an evening or its noon, because the terror makes the duration seem short; this means less than a full day.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.anchor: استقلوا مدة لبثهم فى الدنيا لما عاينوا من الهول كقوله لم يلبثوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.claim: “The noon of the evening” is licensed by the two periods' relation within one day: their stay did not reach an entire day, only one end of it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.anchor: وإنما صحت اضافة الضحى إلى العشية للملابسة بينهما لاجتماعهما فى نهار واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.claim: The passage answers those who claim the afterlife involves only spiritual comfort or pain without sensation.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.anchor: الآية رد على من قال: أحوال الآخرة غير محسوسة، وإنما هي راحة الروح أو تألمها

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r2.claim: The people who see the Hour are disbelievers, who feel their worldly stay was no more than part of a day.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.claim: The phrase means an afternoon, or the morning following that afternoon, minimizing the apparent length of worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.anchor: أي قدر عشية { أو ضحاها } أي أو قدر الضحا الذي يلي تلك العشية، والمراد تقليل مدة الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.claim: They will think they remained in the world for one day only.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.anchor: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا يوما واحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.claim: Alternatively, they mean they stayed in their graves only through an afternoon or its morning, having underestimated it after seeing the terror.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.anchor: وقيل: «لم يلبثوا» في قبورهم «إلا عشية أو ضحاها»، وذلك أنهم استقصروا مدة لبثهم

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.claim: Although morning ordinarily precedes afternoon, Arabs may pair one with the other to mean the same day's opposite end, as in customary appointments.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.anchor: ولكن أضيف الضحا إلى العشية، وهو اليوم الذي يكون فيه على عادة العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r7.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r7.claim: A poem says they attacked at the evening of the new moon or its sirr, meaning the evening's final hidden phase; it supports the idiom.

ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.claim: In ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā, the final alif and hāʾ refer to ʿashiyyah: “an evening or its forenoon,” with the forenoon annexed to the evening.
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.anchor: هذه الألف والهاء عائدة على (عشية)، المعنى إلا عشية أو ضحاها.

ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.claim: Morning, evening, and forenoon belong to their day: “morning and its evening” is followed by that day’s evening, whereas “evening and its morning” means the following morning.
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.anchor: والغداة والعشي والضحوة والضحى لليوم الذي يكون فيه،

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.claim: When they see what was promised, worldly life will seem to have lasted only an hour, as in 46:35.
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.anchor: كأنهم لم يلبثوا في الدنيا إلا ساعة من نهار

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says the final pronoun in duhaha is an additive particle: they stayed only an evening or a morning.
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس : الهاء والألف صلة للكلام

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj understand 'its morning' as the morning of the day whose evening is named; Arabic can say 'evening or its morning.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : المراد بإضافة الضحى إلى العشية إضافتها إلى يوم العشية

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.speaker: النحويون
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.claim: The grammarians allow an annexation based on the slightest relation: an earlier morning may be called the morning of its later evening; the ordeal is called evening and relief its morning.
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.anchor: يكفي في حسن الإضافة أدنى سبب

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.claim: The final verses answer disbelievers who taunted the Prophet for not knowing when the Hour would arrive.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.anchor: respond to the disbelievers who chided the Prophet for not knowing when the Hour would come

STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.claim: Most commentators say the time in the grave will seem brief before the resurrection and gathering before God.
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.anchor: Most commentators say that this verse means that the time in the grave will seem short

STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.claim: Others say earthly life will seem like only an hour compared with the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.anchor: Others say the implication is that life on earth will seem as if it were only an hour

STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.claim: Here morning is said to represent worldly life as people see the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.anchor: morning (ḍuḥā) is said to refer to the time period of the worldly life

ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.claim: Like several other verses, this indicates that earthly time is an illusory concept that loses meaning in the ultimate reality of the hereafter.
ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.anchor: a subtle indication of the illusory, earthbound nature of man's concept of "time" - a concept which, we are told, will lose all its meaning

TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.claim: On seeing the Hour, the deniers will feel they spent only an evening or its morning in worldly life; Arabs use morning and evening for the first and last parts of a day.
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.anchor: فكذلك قوله: {إلا عشية أو ضحاها} [النازعات: 46] إنما معناها إلا آخر يوم أو أوله

TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says worldly life will seem brief in their eyes when they encounter the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.anchor: وقت الدنيا في أعين القوم حين عاينوا الآخرة

TABATABAI:79:46/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r5.claim: The comparison means that worldly life until resurrection will seem as brief as one afternoon or its morning, like a portion of one day.
TABATABAI:79:46/r5.anchor: بأن قرب الساعة من حياتهم الدنيا بحيث مثلهم حين يرونها مثلهم لو لبثوا بعد حياتهم في الأرض عشية أو ضحى تلك العشية

TABATABAI:79:46/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r6.claim: The “sojourn” is the interval from worldly life to resurrection, meaning the grave period; counting the whole worldly life for judgment supports this reading.
TABATABAI:79:46/r6.anchor: أن المراد باللبث لبث ما بين الحياه الدنيا والبعث أي لبثهم في القبور

TABATABAI:79:46/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:46/r7.claim: One alternative makes the sojourn the interval from asking about the Hour until resurrection; the author objects that people witness the interval only at resurrection and that death, not their question, precedes it.
TABATABAI:79:46/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد به اللبث بين حين سؤالهم عن وقتها وبين البعث

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.claim: The author cites 23:114, which asks how many years people remained on Earth, while rejecting worldly life as the meaning of the brief sojourn.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.anchor: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.claim: The Qummi commentary says the period was part of a day.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.anchor: عشية أو ضحاها } قال بعض يوم

TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.claim: “Its forenoon” is annexed to the evening of the same day; morning and evening expressions imply adjoining periods.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.anchor: وقوله أو ضحاها أضاف الضحى إلى العشية والغداة والعشي والضحوة والضحي لليوم

TABRISI:79:45-46/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:79:45-46/r14.claim: When people see the Resurrection, the world will seem so short that they will think they spent only an afternoon or its morning there.

THALABI:v10p129/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p129/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p129/r1.claim: When people see the Resurrection, they will feel they had remained in the world—or perhaps in their graves—only an evening or its early morning.
THALABI:v10p129/r1.anchor: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا في الدنيا قيل: في قبورهم، إلا عشية أو ضحاها

THALABI:v10p129/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p129/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p129/r2.claim: Al-Farra notes that evening has no literal duha; the phrase is an Arabic way of saying the end or beginning of a day.
THALABI:v10p129/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: ليس للغاشية ضحى إنما الضحى لصدر النهار

THALABI:v10p129/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p129/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p129/r3.claim: A line by a Banu Uqayl poet uses ʿashiyyat al-hilal for the evening when the new moon is hidden.
THALABI:v10p129/r3.anchor: نحن صبحنا عامرا في دارها … جردا تعاطى طرفي نهارها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.claim: The people meant are the disbelievers of Quraysh, and seeing the Resurrection makes worldly life seem very short.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.anchor: {كأنهم} يعني كفار قريش. {يوم يرونها} يعاينون القيامة. {لم يلبثوا} في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.claim: They will have spent only part of a day either in their graves or in worldly life, like the last part or beginning of a day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: يقول لم يمكثوا في قبورهم، ولا في الدنيا إلا قدر آخر نهار أو أوله (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.claim: The final hāʾ and alif in ḍuḥāhā are grammatical extensions; the sense is only an evening or morning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: الهاء، والألف صلة للكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.claim: They explain ḍuḥāhā as the morning of the evening's day, like the Arabic expression evening or its next morning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.anchor: والعرب تقول: آتيك العشية أو غداتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.claim: When they see what they denied, they will feel as if they had only stayed in the world for an hour before it passed away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أن ما أنكروه سيرونه حتى كأنهم لم يزالوا فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.claim: At its sight, people will think they spent only an evening or morning in their graves, underestimating the time because of the terror they see.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.anchor: { كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا } في قبورهم { إلا عشية أو ضحاها } أي: نهارها

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.claim: At the Hour, worldly life will seem no longer than an evening or its forenoon; life passes quickly, the cautious escape its terrors, and the heedless reach everlasting calamity.
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.anchor: Uzun zannedilen dünya ömrü o kadar çabuk geçer

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.claim: After returning to life, people will see how brief worldly life was beside the everlasting afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.anchor: İnsanlar, ikinci hayata döndüklerinde ebedî olan âhirete göre geçici olan dünya hayatının ne kadar kısa olduğunu anlayacaklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.claim: Psychologically, the past seems short because it is finished; the open, uncertain future feels more important and interesting and can cause anxiety.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.anchor: Psikolojik olarak insana geçmiş daima kısa bir zamanmış gibi gelir; çünkü geçmiş artık olmuş bitmiştir
